transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-24 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Rina (Zephyr), Tom (Zephyr), Priya (Zephyr)

Summary (auto): quick sync on cache metrics and a plan for a tune + soak.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh let's kick off. we left off last week with the lower-than-expected kv hit rate on the checkout flow, right?
[00:10] Rina: yeah, thanks maya. still seeing about 18% effective kv hit overall, but when we do user-level flows it jumps to like 38% for repeat shoppers, so it's inconsistent.
[00:22] Ethan: mhm, and the distribution looked pretty tail-heavy — a few long sessions with big context causing eviction of useful keys. we think TTL and the prefixing strategy are the main culprits.
[00:36] Tom: quick note — we did enable the session affinity flag you suggested, but we also have aggressive request fan-out in our middleware which may be nuking the cache.
[00:48] Maya: ok so two threads: engineering changes on zephyr's side to reduce fan-out, and server-side tuning from us — ttl, prefetch thresholds, and prompt canonicalization.
[00:59] Priya: when you say prompt canonicalization, can you give a concrete example? cause our product texts vary a lot by region and promo banners.
[01:12] Ethan: yeah totally. so instead of sending full UI copy each time, we create a small template key — like a template id + a normalized slot map — that lets the kv key match across similar prompts. so 'show me deals' vs 'show me today's deals' map to same prefix.
[01:32] Rina: oh right, we tried slug-based templates but it was brittle. is there a recommended tolerance for token differences?
[01:42] Ethan: not exact, but the approach we recommended last week was a two-layer hash: short canonical prefix + second-level fingerprint for slot values. if the prefix matches, you get a cached completion and then apply the slots. avoids recomputing completions for trivial variants.
[01:58] Tom: that sounds promising. any risk to hallucination if the slot substitution isn't applied correctly?
[02:06] Ethan: small risk, we should do a validation pass — run asserts on the slot-output mapping. also set a low safety TTL for those template keys while testing.
[02:18] Jordan: i can add a QA step to the runbook, like sample asserts and a regression prompt set.
[02:25] Rina: metrics review — we pulled the shared sheet you sent, thanks. couple things: peak hour shows kv hits collapse to ~9%, off-peak sits at ~36%. batch sizes pulsing up during peak increases latency and causes more eviction.
[02:42] Maya: right that's the continuous batching effect — bigger batches use more memory per request and reduce effective kv capacity. we proposed two mitigations: dynamic batch caps during peak and a prioritized prefix cache for checkout flows.
[02:56] Priya: prioritized prefix cache — is that something you do at model-router level?
[03:03] Ethan: yeah at routing we can pin certain route prefixes to a small LRU region with higher retention. think of it as a hot-slab that is protected from full eviction when general memory spikes happen.
[03:16] Priya: makes sense. what's the cost delta on reserved vs hot-slab.
[03:20] Maya: minimal configuration cost; might increase memory footprint slightly but should be small compared to overall GPU RAM. we'll quantify in the config doc.
[03:30] Tom: we also wanted to ask about prefetch heuristics — last week you mentioned a 'warm start' option. can you recap?
[03:39] Ethan: yeah warm-start prefetch basically primes the kv for expected next-turns based on the route and typical user flows. for checkout the router prefetches likely completions for 'shipping options' and 'promo code' slots when session userid shows intent. reduces the first-turn miss penalty.
[03:59] Rina: last time prefetch bumped hit-rate by ~5% in a synthetic run, but introduced extra writes and some noise. how do we balance write amplification?
[04:10] Ethan: we tune prefetch aggressiveness and only prefetch keys that pass a confidence threshold — and use a soft ttl so prefetch keys expire faster if unused. also allow prefetch to be sampled (e.g., 30% of sessions) during pilot.
[04:26] Priya: cool. which exact config will you share?
[04:30] Maya: we'll share the eviction policy, prefetch JSON, and a short patch for prompt canonicalization. ethan will attach example traces.
[04:39] Rina: walked thru the error logs — a couple of 503s coincide with our peak when you had larger batches. any immediate remediation?
[04:47] Ethan: we can reduce max batch latency target and enable fallback to a cheaper model variant for tail requests to keep latency SLOs. it's the same fallback policy we used for the demo last quarter but tuned for zephyr traffic.
[04:59] Tom: fallback to cheaper variant — any impact on output quality for checkout? we can't have price-safety regressions.
[05:07] Ethan: fallback variant is same architecture but lower sequence-length optimization; we'll add a regression test set for critical checkout prompts. if fallback fails quality gates, we fail-over to full model but with degraded latency.
[05:21] Priya: ok. timeline and responsibilities?
[05:24] Maya: i mapped them — action items listed in the doc. high-priority: ethan send config, maya send pricing/runbook, tom enable traffic-mirroring for the soak.
[05:35] Rina: about soak — do you want production traffic mirrored or synthetic replay?
[05:40] Ethan: mirror is better for real distributions, but replay helps isolate variables. we recommend mirror + sampled replay for edge cases.
[05:50] Tom: we can do mirror at 10% to start.
[05:53] Maya: perfect. any other blockers?
[05:55] Rina: security sign-off — we still need the updated SOC 2 artifact and KMS flow doc.
[06:02] Jordan: noted, i'll attach SOC 2 summary and KMS flow to the runbook and send to priya by tomorrow.
[06:08] Priya: thanks. quick question — do you support customer-managed keys in the private plane? we need HSM for PII.
[06:17] Ethan: yes for private we support KMS/HSM integrations. there's a short setup checklist; we'll include it. for hosted we offer envelope encryption and managed KMS.
[06:28] Rina: nice. small nit — in the metrics sheet there's an odd spike labeled 'unknown', likely instrumentation mismatch. we'll reconcile offline.
[06:36] Tom: one last technical — is kv eviction deterministic or guided by sequence-length heuristics?
[06:42] Ethan: eviction is LRU-ish but guided: large keys (long sequences) get a weight to make them less likely to evict small high-value prefixes; this is configurable in the eviction policy.
[06:55] Rina: ok good to know.
[07:00] Maya: let's recap next steps quickly — maya will share runbook + pricing by thursday; ethan will post config and example traces; tom will enable 10% mirror for soak and run the soak through monday; jordan will send security artifacts.
[07:20] Priya: can we also add a short acceptance criteria doc — e.g., kv hit-rate >= 35% for checkout, checkout median p95 latency < 350ms, zero critical regressions in QA test set?
[07:33] Maya: yep we can draft that and include in the pilot success criteria.
[07:38] Rina: great, thanks everyone.
[07:41] Maya: thanks all, we'll reconvene next Tuesday same time.

References: shared spreadsheet: https://app.shortlink/zephyr/cache-metrics-0324, runbook draft: https://docs.redwood/reports/zephyr-runbook-draft (links shared in chat).

End of transcript
